definition: A travelling vibration that transfers energy from one place to another without transferring matter.
A line joining neighbouring points on the same crest of a wave; wavefronts are at right angles to the direction of travel and one wavelength apart.
The distance from a point on one wave to the same point on the next wave, such as crest to crest; symbol $\lambda$, measured in m.
The number of complete waves passing a point, or the number of vibrations made, each second; symbol $f$, measured in hertz (Hz).
The greatest distance a point on a wave moves from its rest position; on a transverse wave, from the rest position to a crest (not crest to trough).
The distance a wave travels each second; symbol $v$, in m/s, with $v = f\lambda$.
A wave in which the vibration is at right angles to the direction of travel, such as light and other electromagnetic radiation, water waves and seismic S-waves.
A wave in which the vibration is parallel to the direction of travel, such as sound and seismic P-waves.
A wave bouncing back off a surface, keeping the same speed, frequency and wavelength.
The change in direction of a wave that meets a boundary at an angle and changes speed as it crosses it; its frequency stays the same.
The spreading out of waves as they pass through a gap or round an edge, with no change in wavelength; through a gap it is greatest when the gap is about one wavelength wide.
A shallow tray of water, lit from above, in which a vibrating bar makes water waves so you can watch reflection, refraction and diffraction.
